title: Travelling salesman

problem.name: Travelling salesman
problem.statement_latex:
Given a weighted graph $G=(V,E,w)$, $|V|=n$, find a Hamiltonian cycle $C$ minimizing $\sum_{e\in C}w(e)$, or report infeasibility. Integer weights are binary encoded and have maximum magnitude $L$. The problem models routing and cyclic sequencing.

\entryalias{17}\textbf{Directed minimum feedback arc set.} Given a directed graph $D=(V,A)$, find a minimum-cardinality $F\subseteq A$ such that $(V,A\setminus F)$ is acyclic. Equivalently, minimize the number of backward arcs in a vertex order; nonnegative weights give the weighted objective. This models ranking with inconsistent pairwise preferences.

The general quantum bounds use QRAM time, bounded-degree travelling-salesman bounds use gate time, and classical bounds use RAM time with polynomial costs for weight arithmetic.

quantum.headline_latex: $O^*(1.728^n)$ for both problems, quantum subset dynamic programming; $O^*(1.110^n)$ and $O^*(1.301^n)$ for degree-three and degree-four travelling salesman, quantum backtracking.
quantum.details_latex: The common dynamic-programming construction precomputes partial subset values and uses quantum minimum finding over their decompositions. For feedback arc set, an ordered partition fixes every crossing arc's contribution and leaves two internal ordering costs. For travelling salesman, the state also records path endpoints. These constructions assume coherent access to exponential tables. The bounded-degree travelling-salesman algorithms use polynomial workspace and include factors $\log L\log\log L$ for integer weights.

classical.headline_latex: $O(n^2 2^n)$ for travelling salesman, Held--Karp; $O^*(2^n)$ for feedback arc set, subset dynamic programming.
classical.details_latex: Held--Karp stores the shortest path for each visited set and endpoint in $O(n2^n)$ words. The feedback-arc recurrence stores the best ordering cost for each vertex subset. Both use exponential memory. For degree-three and degree-four travelling salesman, sparse-graph path decompositions improve the bounds to $O^*(1.1757^n)$ and $O^*(1.4214^n)$ with exponential memory; a polynomial-space cubic-graph comparator takes $O^*(1.232^n)$. The weighted sparse-graph construction retains polynomial weight-bit costs. Restricted feedback-arc inputs, such as tournaments, select their own specialized classical algorithms.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedups through smaller exponential constants. The common subset dynamic program uses minimum finding and amplitude amplification; bounded-degree travelling salesman uses quantum backtracking in the specified graph and memory regimes.

hardware.description_latex: The general algorithms combine polynomial active registers with exponential QRAM. Bounded-degree travelling salesman uses polynomial logical workspace and exponentially long coherent tree searches. Useful implementations require fault tolerance and reversible objective arithmetic.
